original_evidence.text: | WoeUSB-ng | https://github.com/WoeUSB/WoeUSB-ng | cc52ffc / 2026-01-25 | N (no self-update) | Y (silent, automatic during normal "create bootable USB" workflow) | Y (downloads and writes a UEFI bootloader image executed by firmware at boot) | https, cert validation enforced (default `urllib.request`, no `ssl.CERT_NONE`/`check_hostname=False` found anywhere in the codebase) | N | none — file is written to the boot partition with zero hash/signature check | server-supplied/unpinned (trusts whatever bytes GitHub raw returns) | `src/WoeUSB/core.py:375` `urllib.request.urlretrieve("https://github.com/pbatard/rufus/raw/master/res/uefi/uefi-ntfs.img", "uefi-ntfs.img")` inside `install_uefi_ntfs_support_partition()` (`core.py:361`), whose own docstring admits: "FIXME: Currently this requires internet access to download the image from GitHub directly, it should be replaced by including the image in our datadir." The downloaded file is `shutil.copy2()`'d straight onto the UEFI:NTFS boot partition (`core.py:381`) with no checksum or signature check — a compromised GitHub raw CDN or a MITM of that one HTTPS connection (if TLS is ever broken) directly yields a malicious UEFI bootloader on the target device. |
